# Supplementary text

Additional details regarding the cleaning process are provided in the `Remark` and `Age justification` columns of *Dataset S1*.

## Taxonomic decisions

Given that *Lagostomus (Lagostomopsis)* is a subgenus [@rasia2012], we set the `genus` column of each *Lagostomus (Lagostomopsis)* occurrence to *Lagostomus*, and switched their `genus_level_status` from `extinct` to `extant`.

All specimens referred to as *Lagostomus cavifrons*, *L. debilis*, *L. egenus*, *L. heterogenidens* and *L. minimus* were synonymised with *Lagostomus maximus*, following [@ubilla2016; @rasia_vizcacha_2024].

Following @busker2019, we added two occurrences of *Saremmys ligcura* from the two localities of Bryn Gwyn and Gran Barranca (Chubut, Argentina).

We incorporated four occurrences -- corresponding to four different taxa -- from the AMD-45 locality (18.9--17.1 Ma) published by @arnal2026: *Maquiamys praecursor*, *Manumys materdei*, *Marianamys altadens* and *Peruchinchilla prima*.

We followed the latest taxonomic revisions proposed by @rasia2026 regarding the hyperdiverse dinomyid fauna from the Ituzaingó Formation (Late Miocene).

## Age of the localities/formations

The age ranges of the Miocene occurrences from the Río Santa Cruz (Santacrucian SALMA) were sharpened based on their assigned locality [@arnal2019]. Hence, occurrence from Barrancas Blancas and Segundas Barrancas Blancas were respectively assigned the 16.49--17.45 and 15.63--16.46 Ma intervals [@fernicola2019].

The single occurrence assigned to *Lagostomus striatus* was removed as considered *nomen nodum* by @rasia2016.

The age of the Ituzaingó formation was set to Huayquerian SALMA (Late Miocene), *ca*. 5--8 Ma [@romano2023].

The age range of occurrences from @bucher2021 were set to the one of the original publication: 14.6--12.75 Ma when coming from the "Cruces Infinitos" and "Los Yeguarizos localities", 12.75--12.05 Ma when coming from the "La Gloria" and "La Hoyada" localities.

Based on @brandoni2016, the age range of the occurrences from the Pinturas fauna [*e*.*g*., @kramarz2002; -@kramarz2004; -@kramarz2006], Burdigalian, were set between 20 and 16.8 Ma.

The age range of the occurrences belonging to the Andalhualá Formation was set to Huayquerian--Chapadmalalan, *ca*. 7.14--3.66 Ma [@esteban2014; -@esteban2019].

The age range of the occurrences belonging to the Sierra Baguales (Santa Cruz formation, Magallanes, Chile) were set to 19--17.8 Ma according to the isotopic constraints provided in @bostelmann2013.

The age range of the occurrences reported from the Cerro Boleadoras Formation was set to 16.5--15.1 Ma, according to @vizcaino2022.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Load kableExtra library
library(kableExtra)
# Function to convert elements of a table cell to bold
convert_bold <- function(el){
  return(paste0("**", el, "**"))
}
# Load additional libraries
library(readxl)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-DDperf
#| tbl-cap: "Performance of the different network architectures tested in our DeepDive analyses. `LSTM Layers` and `Fully-connected` are respectively the number of Long Short Term Memory and Fully-connected units of the network (3: 128, 64 and 32 nodes; 2: 64 and 32 nodes; 1: 32 nodes). `Dropout` represents the Monte-Carlo dropout fraction, that is, the proportion of connections between neurons randomly toggled off between two learning epochs -- one epoch being characterised by a complete pass through the entire training dataset −, preventing from overfitting. `Nb. training epochs` is the optimal number of training epochs. `Training loss` and `Validation loss` are the values of the Mean Squared Error (MSE) estimated between the 'true' diversity of each simulated dataset (resp. from the training or the validation set), and the predicted diversity made by the network after $n$ rounds of optimisation, where $n$ is the optimal number of training epochs. `Evaluation loss` represent the MSE between each true and its associated predicted diversity trajectory from the test datset, once the is trained (*i*.*e*., after $n$ rounds of optimisation, where $n$ is the optimal number of training epochs). The optimal number of epochs is determined when the `Validation loss` starts increasing (see @fig-ddHistPlotL2D2 and @fig-ddHistPlotL3D2). Architectures resulting in the smallest evaluation loss values, *i*.*e*., generating the most accurate predictions, are depicted in bold."

tbl_dd <- read.csv("../Data/supp_tbl/dd_network_perf.csv")
colnames(tbl_dd) <- c("LSTM layers", "Fully-connected", "Dropout", "Nb. training epochs", "Training loss", "Validation loss", "Evaluation loss")
# Turn to bold best architectures
tbl_dd[1,] <- sapply(tbl_dd[1,], FUN = convert_bold)
tbl_dd[3,] <- sapply(tbl_dd[3,], FUN = convert_bold)
# Display
kable(tbl_dd, align = 'c')
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: tbl_PhyloHPD
#| tbl-cap: Table representing the lower and upper bounds of the 95% HPD (resp. 'q_2.5%' and 'q_97.5%') of the distribution of the divergence ages leading to all the extant chinchilloid species absent from the fossil record -- *i*.*e*., all species but *Lagostomus maximus*. Ages are expressed in Ma.

tbl <- read.table("../Data/supp_tbl/95pct_HPD_tbl.txt", header = T)
# Add space and italicise species names
colnames(tbl) <- sapply(X = colnames(tbl),
                        FUN = function(x){
                          gensp <- gsub(x, pattern = "_", replacement = " ")
                          return(paste0("*", gensp, "*"))
                          })
# Round values
tbl <- apply(X = tbl,
             FUN = round,
             MARGIN = c(1,2),
             digits = 2)
# Indicate row names
rownames(tbl) <- c("q_2.5%", "q_97.5%")
# Display
kable(tbl, align = "c")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-cv_sp
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficient of speciation rate variation across the 10 BDNN replicates with random trait (*i*.*e*., body mass and/or hypsodonty index) imputation for taxa with missing trait reconstruction ($n=11$), excluding Caribbean taxa. Simulated values (`cv_simulated`) were obtained from the analysis of 100 simulated datasets matching the empirical datasets in terms of number of traits, clade age and (approximately) number of extant species, generated under a constant-rate birth-death model. Empirical values (`cv_empirical`) were obtained from the analysis of the empirical dataset. *Note: significant variations of speciation rate across lineages imply `cv_empirical` > `cv_expected`*."

# Load and adapt table
cv_tbl_sp <- readRDS("../Data/supp_tbl/BDNN_imputation_NoCar/coeff_speciation_rate_variation_across_replicates_NoCar.RDS")
cv_tbl_sp$replicate[nrow(cv_tbl_sp)] <- "Mean"
colnames(cv_tbl_sp)[3] <- "Replicate"
cv_tbl_sp <- cv_tbl_sp %>% 
  mutate(cv_empirical = as.numeric(cv_empirical), cv_expected = as.numeric(cv_expected)) %>% 
  mutate(cv_empirical = sapply(X = cv_empirical, FUN = round, digits = 2)) %>% 
  mutate(cv_expected = sapply(X = cv_expected, FUN = round, digits = 2))
cv_tbl_sp[nrow(cv_tbl_sp), ] <- sapply(X = cv_tbl_sp[nrow(cv_tbl_sp), ],
                                       FUN = convert_bold)

# Display
kable(cv_tbl_sp, align = "c")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-cv_ex
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficient of extinction rate variation across the 10 BDNN replicates with random trait (*i*.*e*., body mass and/or hypsodonty index) imputation for taxa with missing trait reconstruction ($n=11$), excluding caribbean taxa. *Note: significant variations of speciation rate across lineages imply `cv_empirical` > `cv_expected`*."

# Load and adapt table
cv_tbl_ex <- readRDS("../Data/supp_tbl/BDNN_imputation_NoCar/coeff_extinction_rate_variation_across_replicates_NoCar.RDS")
cv_tbl_ex$replicate[nrow(cv_tbl_ex)] <- "Mean"
colnames(cv_tbl_ex)[3] <- "Replicate"
cv_tbl_ex <- cv_tbl_ex %>% 
  mutate(cv_empirical = as.numeric(cv_empirical), cv_expected = as.numeric(cv_expected)) %>% 
  mutate(cv_empirical = sapply(X = cv_empirical, FUN = round, digits = 2)) %>% 
  mutate(cv_expected = sapply(X = cv_expected, FUN = round, digits = 2))
cv_tbl_ex[nrow(cv_tbl_ex), ] <- sapply(X = cv_tbl_ex[nrow(cv_tbl_ex), ],
                                       FUN = convert_bold)
# Display
kable(cv_tbl_ex, align = "c")

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-pred_imp_ex
#| tbl-cap: Predictor importance on extinction rate across the 10 BDNN replicates with random trait (*i*.*e*., body mass and/or hypsodonty index) imputation for taxa with missing trait reconstruction ($n=11$) after excluding caribbean taxa. We highlighted in bold the three factors that contribute the most to variations in extinction rates across species.

# Load
pred_imp_tbl_ex <- readRDS("../Data/supp_tbl/BDNN_imputation_NoCar/BDNN_predictor_importance_ex_rate_NoCar.RDS")
pred_imp_tbl_ex$Predictor[which(pred_imp_tbl_ex$Predictor == "Hypsodonty")] <- "Crown_Height"
pred_imp_tbl_ex <- pred_imp_tbl_ex[order(pred_imp_tbl_ex$OverallRank), ]
rownames(pred_imp_tbl_ex) <- 1:nrow(pred_imp_tbl_ex)
# Make it clearer
colnames(pred_imp_tbl_ex) <- gsub("^Replicate_", "R. ", colnames(pred_imp_tbl_ex))
pred_imp_tbl_ex <- pred_imp_tbl_ex %>% rename(Rank = "OverallRank")
# Highlight the podium
pred_imp_tbl_ex[1:3, c("Predictor", "Rank")] <- apply(X = pred_imp_tbl_ex[1:3, c("Predictor", "Rank")],
                                                      FUN = convert_bold,
                                                      MARGIN = c(1,2))
# Display
kable(pred_imp_tbl_ex, align = "c")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-FC_BM

The 'Total' row shows the averaged values across the 10 replicates.

tbl <- readRDS("../Data/supp_tbl/BDNN_imputation_NoCar/Fold_change_S_XL_across_replicates.RDS")

tbl[nrow(tbl), ] <- sapply(X = tbl[nrow(tbl), ], FUN = convert_bold)

```
